entries.title: Chōjū-jinbutsu-giga
entries.note: Proto-manga milestone: sequential ink scrolls depicting animals and humans with motion and visual storytelling.

entries.title: Hokusai Manga (北斎漫画), Volume I
entries.note: First widespread use of the term 'manga' for informal sketch collections; directly shaped how the word is used today.

entries.title: Rakuten Kitazawa — Tagosaku to Mokube no Tokyo Kenbutsu
entries.note: Widely cited as an early modern manga/comic strip milestone — panel-based sequential storytelling in a Japanese newspaper.

entries.title: Katsudō Shashin (Matsumoto fragment)
entries.note: A short animated filmstrip widely cited as the oldest known Japanese animation fragment (exact dating debated).

entries.title: Namakura Gatana (The Dull Sword)
entries.note: Among the oldest surviving Japanese animated shorts; early example of comedic animation by Seitaro Kitayama.

entries.title: Momotaro: Sacred Sailors
entries.note: First Japanese feature-length animated film (wartime context); produced by Seo Mitsuyo at Shochiku.

entries.title: The White Snake Enchantress (Hakujaden)
entries.note: First Japanese colour animated feature film; Toei Animation's theatrical debut — set the studio system template.

entries.title: Astro Boy TV series premieres
entries.note: First Japanese TV animation produced as an ongoing weekly series; Tezuka Osamu's studio Mushi Production defined the format.

entries.title: Doraemon begins serialisation
entries.note: One of the longest-running and highest-selling manga series in history; over 100 million volumes sold worldwide.

entries.title: Lupin III manga serialisation begins
entries.note: Monkey Punch's Lupin III helped define adult-oriented action manga and later launched a major anime franchise.

entries.title: Dragon Ball begins serialisation (Weekly Shōnen Jump)
entries.note: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball became one of the defining shōnen franchises globally; over 260 million volumes sold.

entries.title: Akira begins serialisation
entries.note: Katsuhiro Otomo's Akira was a landmark in detailed background art and cinematic panel composition; widely credited with bringing manga to Western audiences.

entries.title: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind manga begins
entries.note: Hayao Miyazaki's manga later became the springboard for Studio Ghibli; renowned for environmental world-building.

entries.title: Slam Dunk begins serialisation
entries.note: Takehiko Inoue's Slam Dunk is widely credited with boosting basketball popularity in Japan; a benchmark for dynamic action linework.

entries.title: One Piece begins serialisation
entries.note: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece is the best-selling manga series of all time, with over 530 million volumes in circulation worldwide.

entries.title: Naruto begins serialisation
entries.note: Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto became one of the defining manga of the 2000s global boom; over 250 million copies sold.

entries.title: Sailor Moon begins serialisation
entries.note: Naoko Takeuchi's Sailor Moon became a defining shōjo franchise internationally and a major influence on magical girl storytelling.

entries.title: Attack on Titan begins serialisation
entries.note: Hajime Isayama's Attack on Titan became a global phenomenon and one of the top-selling manga series of the 2010s.
